name: Landmine Press
description: The landmine press is a shoulder pressing exercise where one end of a barbell is anchored to the floor (in a landmine attachment or corner) while the other end is pressed overhead in a natural arc. The angled pressing path is shoulder-friendly compared to vertical overhead pressing, making it an excellent option for lifters with shoulder impingement or limited shoulder mobility while still providing significant anterior deltoid and triceps stimulus.

execution.starting_position: Anchor one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment or wedge it in a corner. Kneel or stand facing the barbell's loaded end, holding it at shoulder height with one hand (or both hands clasped together).
execution.setup_instructions: Insert one end of a barbell into a landmine base or secure it in a corner on a mat. Load the opposite end with appropriate weight. Kneel or stand facing the loaded end.
steps: Step 1: Hold the end of the barbell at shoulder height with the hand of the pressing side. Stagger your stance or kneel for stability.
Step 2: Brace the core firmly. The barbell will arc forward and upward on a fixed path.
Step 3: Exhale and press the barbell end upward and forward in its natural arc until the arm is fully extended.
Step 4: Inhale and lower back down along the same arc to shoulder height. Complete reps, then switch sides.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the press; inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Letting the torso rotate as you press — brace to resist rotation
Pressing straight up rather than allowing the barbell to follow its natural arc
safety_considerations: The angled path is naturally shoulder-friendly, but stop if pain is felt at any point
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Press to full arm extension along the arc; return to shoulder height.
coaching_cues: Let the bar's natural arc guide your press — don't fight it
Squeeze your core like a vise throughout the movement
